notes:
I couldn't write the Jeremiah 23 notes. The research tool shut down on my first attempt, before any pages loaded, so I have no source material.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Writing the verse-by-verse notes now would mean doing exactly that, so I've left them out.

These are the pages I was trying to read first:
- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** the Enduring Word page on Jeremiah 23, and the Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and Gill entries on Bible Hub.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** v. 6 ("The LORD Our Righteousness") looked like the main candidate. John Wesley preached a sermon on this verse, which is hosted on wesley.nnu.edu. It could be set against Reformed and Baptist teaching on imputed righteousness from ligonier.org, monergism.com and spurgeon.org. Lutheran sources (1517.org, lcms.org) could also cover v. 29, where God's word is like a hammer.
- **Other views:** the NET Bible notes for modern scholarship, and newadvent.org or catholic.com for Catholic readings of the "Branch" in v. 5. For the prophetic dreams in vv. 25–32, I'd check charismatic writers on samstorms.org and pneumareview.com.

If you ask again, I'll start with those pages and write the notes with a URL for every point.
